newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-June 2.

text.p: There are 29 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- APPLE DAILY said Hong Kong people should fight for freedom and democracy themselves and not rely on politicians. Eight years ago, many politicians supported the pro-democracy movement, but now most have changed and joined the opposite camp. The paper said whether the June 4 parade remembering the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown could be held next year would measure the level of freedom here, and if people were deprived of this freedom, that would be the end of Hong Kong, it said.

-- The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said the attitude of Britain towards the handover was different from that of Asian countries who had shown more enthusiasm and support. It said the British governmnnt still wanted to raise anti-China forces and interfere in Hong Kong affairs after the handover. The paper said London should adjust its policies in the remaining 29 days, because China would not give in an inch when it came to the issue of sovereignty.

-- The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said there would not be a single day this month without some joyous events to mark the end of colonial rule and the reunification with China. However, the paper said, a culture was needed in which all events could be marked in a peaceful manner. People should be free to toast the reunification or to march peacefully in memory of Tiananmen. That should always remain the Hong Kong spirit, the paper said.
